out.rationale: Arnesen et al. report that language-model judges answer more accurately when judging models optimised to win debates, and the authors group their own results with Arnesen et al.'s as part of a body of work that tentatively suggests such techniques may be increasingly viable. The cited passage reports no judge or verifier accuracy result of its own; its tentative statement relies on the results it cites, including Arnesen et al.'s, so DEPENDS_ON rather than ADDRESSES or SUPPORTS. Settings differ: the cited Arnesen et al. passage trains debaters on data generated via self-play for a long-context reading comprehension task judged by language-model evaluators, while the cited passage of the authors concerns neural interactive proofs and names no task.
